issues.title: F5 baseline comparison is not sample-aware — cold-pool rotation makes per-lane counts incomparable
issues.notes: Probe: `bun run script/m14/differential.ts --repo svelte` at 0533251e printed DIFFERENTIAL REGRESSION for svelte:javascript (0->5 unexplained) and svelte:typescript (0->19) while the svelte lane itself stayed 100% covered / 0 unexplained. `evaluateDifferential`'s `comparable` compares only samplePerLang, never WHICH files were drawn, so the #760 cold-pool rotation (prefer never-sampled files) scores a fresh sample against a baseline recorded on a different sample. Consequences: (a) genuine new-sample findings are labelled regressions, (b) the improvement-forcing rule can never be satisfied for corpora larger than the sample without a baseline update. Fix owed: record a per-lane drawn-file-set hash in the baseline; a hash mismatch must report RESAMPLED (triage) instead of REGRESSION. Registered, NOT fixed: this entry dates the finding; the fix wave must land fixture + mutant + spec row (and the oracle mirror where the truth side is the defective one) before any status change. FIXED: sampleSetHash(relPaths) (sha256 of the sorted corpus-relative drawn set) now rides every lane row; --update-baseline pins it per lane into differential-baseline.json hashes; evaluateDifferential compares it and splits one question into three verdicts - same pinned set => strict never-grow (unchanged, still able to fail); different set => RESAMPLED <lane>, excluded from regressions, and the lane's own missing/unexplained anomalies then fail its check for TRIAGE (so a rotated lane can never pass silently on a generous pinned allowance); no pinned set (pre-G5 rows) => strict comparison KEPT plus an unpinnedLanes disclosure, so the gate is not made vacuous for the 154 unrecorded rows at once. Declared-heuristic edges do not fail a resampled lane (they are disclosed as unscored); missing/unexplained do. The claim the run makes is emitted as evidence data.baselineComparison {pinnedLanes,totalBaselineLanes,resampledLanes,unpinnedLanes}. Self-tested in the battery (audit:differential -> script/m14/verify-differential-evidence.ts, 6 cases incl. the rotated-growth case asserted to be triage and never a regression). REMAINING: the file sets are pinned only by the next canonical no-arg --update-baseline run at a stable tree (the same ceremony R2/F1-F9 wait on); until then every lane is disclosed as unpinned and keeps the strict comparison.

issues.title: Groovy GString interpolation is invisible to the graph: 13,830 interpolation sites across 2,115 files emit zero reads, and the nested-quote subset emits a FABRICATED call edge — CLOSED
issues.notes: Found while closing the W21 residual class `GString with a nested double quote inside ${ }` (5 files) - the parse failure is the visible tip. The grammar is grammar(Java, ...) and inherits Java's _string_literal, whose fragment token is `token.immediate(prec(1, /[^\\]+/))` (everything except quote and backslash, which INCLUDES `$` and `{`), and Java's string_interpolation is Java's text-block `'\{'` form. This grammar overrides character_literal, _multiline_string_literal and the multiline fragments, but SEARCHING IT FOR `string_interpolation:` OR `string_fragment` RETURNS NOTHING - so `${...}` and `$name` are opaque literal text by construction and no interpolated identifier can ever reach the analyzer. MEASURED (script/m59/measure-groovy-interpolation.ts, grails-core @ a83f87480e0c, 7,701 *.groovy/*.gradle/*.gsp files, source-matched so the count does not depend on the fix): 2,115 files (27.5%) contain interpolation, 13,830 sites, 59 of them (31 files) are the nested-double-quote subset that fails to PARSE and emits `calls (script) -> X`; 361,280 relationships emitted with 0 contributed by any interpolation site. FAMILY PARITY: dart (DT-F), php, ruby and kotlin all read interpolation and each has a caught `drop-interp-read-uses` mutant; real-groovy-analyzer.ts has ZERO references to interpolation, and no mutant exists because there is no behaviour to mutate. Parse-clean, line-clean, oracle-clean and graph-incomplete, which is why every gate in the repo is green on it. Fix shape recorded in the evidence file: override string_fragment (must stop swallowing `$`), define string_interpolation as `'${' expression '}'` plus the `$identifier` short form, give a bare `$` its own explicit grammar alternative because tree-sitter's regex has no lookahead, check the five existing template_expression conflict entries, add analyzer reads AND the deriveGroovyEdges oracle mirror, and re-cut the W21 residual table afterwards.
issues.resolution: CLOSED 2026-09-16 in seven grammar changes and one analyzer pass (review §6). GRAMMAR: `string_fragment` overridden to stop at `$`; `string_interpolation` = `'${' expression '}'`; the `$name` short form is a TOKEN - as `seq('$', identifier)` the parser stood at `name` where both `identifier` and the inherited `prec(1)` fragment are valid and the fragment won the LEXICAL tie, so `"value $field"` parsed as two fragments (probe-verified against the CLI, fragments at [0,9]-[0,15] and [0,16]-[0,21]); a bare `$` gets its own alternative because tree-sitter's regex has no lookahead, so `/[^"\\$]+|\$(?![{a-zA-Z_])/` is not expressible; the single-quoted forms LOSE the inherited Java alternative, or `'''${x}'''` would interpolate; the `"""` forms carry the same four alternatives; `slashy_string` becomes a RULE that interpolates (measured before the change over 2,000 grails-core files: 154 slashy_string tokens, 3 carrying an interpolation-shaped `$` in 2 files, every one emitting no read - the other 26 `$`-bearing tokens are regex ANCHORS `/^…$/`, which Groovy never interpolates, which is why the fragment stops only at an interpolation-SHAPED `$`). One declared conflict, `[$.map_item, $._unannotated_type]`, closes the parenthesised ARRAY-TYPE map key `[(Byte[]): v]` (an ERROR; `[(Integer): v]` worked only because Integer is also an expression) that left DefaultGraphQLTypeManager.groovy unparsed. ANALYZER: a BARE name in interpolation is read (confidence 0.9, metadata.isInterpolationRead, the identifier's own line) while member and call positions stay owned by the field-access and call walks; behind a local-binding gate (formal/catch parameters, variable declarators, closure `it`, unioned across every enclosing scope, climbing THROUGH nested closures but stopping at the type boundary) - without it the fix would fabricate an edge for every `"$it"` in the corpus. PINS: fixture `groovy/interpolation-reads-g7` holds the contract with its controls in one file (free field read, `$name`, member read, call, bound local/parameter/receiver, nested-closure `def`, implicit `it`, the SINGLE-QUOTED negative control, the raw nested-double-quote form, the slashy free/bound/anchor trio, the array-type map key) with forbidRelationships naming each pre-fix emission; FOUR mutants, all CAUGHT (groovy/drop-interpolation-reads = the exact pre-fix state, interpolation-reads-unbound = the naive fix, interpolation-callee-read = double-emission, interpolation-reads-single-quoted). MEASURED: deterministic 400-file sorted grails-core sample compared SET-WISE, wasm 90c7f39936ba -> fcfead14d8c0: 90 files touched, uses+199, calls+98, ONE loss = `build-logic/settings.gradle calls 44 -> 43`, adjudicated by printing both edge sets (script/m14/tmp/g7-loss-probe.ts) as the deletion of a FABRICATED calls edge whose target was raw recovered text `logger.warn("Build date will be set to (SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH=${System.getenv("` from a line that failed to parse, while the real `calls (script) -> warn@39` stands. The nested-quote class - the parse-visible tip - now parses (hasError false, a real string_interpolation with its inner method_invocation). Why 297 relationships and not 13,830 sites: the sample is 400 files not 7,701, and the binding gate suppresses bound names BY DESIGN. ORACLE MIRROR: deriveGroovyEdges had no interpolation branch at all, so it was green by blindness both before the fix (nothing to see) and after it (nothing to check) - the W20 lesson applied. Mirrored (the same five owning parents, the same bound-name climb, the same `method ?? owner` source rule). The first version asked the weaker question 'is there a method above me?' and a corpus-wide probe over 8,383 groovy files (script/m14/tmp/g7-oracle-mirror-check.ts) reported 4 oracle-only reads in 2 files - every one inside a file that fails to parse as a single whole-file ERROR node, where a Spock feature method is named by a `string_literal` and no class context survives recovery. SECOND INSTRUMENT DEFECT, found because the first canonical F5 run reported grails-core:groovy missing=8 on interpolation-shaped targets: the harness compares only the labels a language's truth derives, and for groovy `uses` was NOT among them (groovy had no read oracle - the limitation the W20 note records as 'a restored read rides the fixture and its mutant but no corpus lane'), so adding interpolation truths injected `uses` edges into a lane that structurally could not match them and EVERY interpolated name became a permanent false MISSING. issues.title: Groovy (#841, M49 G8): a class-level field's dotted continuation aborted the whole class body — parse-failing 384 -> 370 of 6,564, 14 fixed / 0 regressed, 0 files losing a relationship, and the round's two real findings were both INSTRUMENT defects (a fix that passed every hasError check while destroying two files, and a fixture run that shrank the canonical evidence)
issues.notes: Found by opening the m12 census's largest remaining first-error line, which was a bare `}` (57 files) — a recovery point, not a cause. A CLASS-LEVEL FIELD whose initializer continues on lines that begin with a dot (`Path scriptDir = Paths.get(getClass()` / `.protectionDomain` / `.codeSource` / `.location` / `.toURI())` / `.toAbsolutePath()` / `.parent`, grails-core etc/bin/test-bisect.groovy:64; and `Builder b = pm.builder()` / `.excludeTimestamps()` / `.excludeVersion()`, CreateInputObjectTypeBuilder.groovy:38) aborts the whole class body: the declarator ends, delimited, before the first dotted line, a class body had no rule for a bare '.', so the parser inserted MISSING '}' and every later member collapsed with it. The grammar has always allowed this continuation at STATEMENT level (`leading_dot_call`, the W20 contract), so the identical chain inside a method parsed; the fix binds the same node to the field it continues (`repeat($.leading_dot_call)` as a suffix of field_declaration, the delimiter consumed once before the chain), so the analyzer (real-groovy-analyzer L587) and the oracle (differential L1376) consume it unchanged — and it needed one declared conflict ([$._variable_declarator_id, $.scoped_type_identifier]), because with a continuation legal after a declarator the bare `name .` prefix is genuinely ambiguous between a declarator that continues and a scoped type. MEASURED, grails-core @ a83f87480e0c, all 6,564 tracked *.groovy through the production pipeline, identical instrument both sides, only the wasm differing (fcfead14d8c0 -> 5a1d1b21d71f): parse-failing 384 -> 370, the failing-file SETS compared file by file — 14 FIXED, 0 regressed; on the bounded set that could be affected (the 384-file union plus a 400-file deterministic clean control, validation/m59/results/g841-w22-filelist.txt) relationships 57,127 -> 57,354 with 0 files losing a single relationship; `.gradle` a clean null (16 -> 16, 17,248 -> 17,248, byte-identical both sides); parse latency 0.99x (6,564 files, BOTH builds in one process, 0 files slower than 3x — the census wallMs difference is machine contention, not grammar cost). PIN: fixture groovy/class-body-dot-continuation-841 (pre-fix 4 symbols / 18 relationships with the field's calls attributed to the `(script)` pseudo-scope, post-fix 5 / 21 with them owned by the class: the `builder` property did not exist and both control methods had NO owner) plus a wasm-swap NEGATIVE CONTROL, because a compiled grammar cannot be mutated: with the pre-fix wasm the groovy lane reports {"groovy":{"pass":55,"fail":1}} — exactly this fixture, nothing else moving; post-fix 56/0. THE ROUND'S REAL FINDING IS ABOUT INSTRUMENTS: the first implementation offered the continuation as a CLASS-BODY DECLARATION instead — the obvious mirror of the statement-level escape — and it passed every hasError-based instrument (file sets 384 -> 370, 0 regressed, fixture lane green) while silently collapsing TWO files' entire program into a single top-level ERROR node and costing them 18 relationships (220 -> 209, 44 -> 37); both files still 'failed' on both sides, so no failure-set comparison could see it and neither file even contains the target construct. TOML-IDENTITY: a symbol is the FILE (module), a TABLE (namespace) or a KEY (property), and a symbol's NAME is its FULL DOTTED PATH from the document root. Leaf-only naming collides in the first manifest anyone writes — cargo's own has a key named `name` under `[package]` AND under every `[[bin]]`. A segment containing `.`/`"`/`\` is re-quoted, which is TOML's own disambiguation, so `a.b.c` and `"a.b".c` stay distinct. Implied parents are RECORDED in metadata, never materialised: fabricating a table the document never wrote is a guess dressed as a fact. An inline table's keys are part of ONE value expression — a manifest with 200 `{ version = ..., features = [...] }` dependencies would otherwise emit 600+ symbols naming nothing navigable — and their names are kept in `metadata.inlineKeys`, a scoping decision rather than a deletion. A VALUE is data and never a symbol. The module OWNS its name in its own file (html's precedence: `usedNames` starts `{ [moduleName]: 1 }`), because relationships address nodes by name and `doc/book/book.toml` declares `[book]`. The relationship vocabulary is `contains` ALONE, and that is the finding rather than an omission: TOML defines no include, import, alias or reference, so there is no second type any construct could produce, and treating a path-shaped string as a dependency would import ecosystem knowledge into a format that has none. TWO DEFECTS FOUND BY THE CORPUS, neither visible in a hand-written fixture: (1) a quoted key segment containing a dot was indistinguishable from a bare dotted key, so `a.b.c` and `"a.b".c` collapsed to one identity and the dedupe invented a `#2` for a key never declared twice — the unresolvable-identity class arriving through the NAMING SCHEME rather than a missing edge; (2) the module did not own its name, and `doc/book/book.toml` + `doc/contrib/book.toml` (2 collisions in 684 files) made every `contains` edge naming `book` resolve to two nodes. issues.title: svelte wave 1: ERROR/MISSING classification, the anonymous-node read, the D7/D8 call rulings, rune-invocation edges, the store seam, and the M12 uses/references audit
issues.notes: THE LANE HAD NO LEDGER ROW AT ALL, which is itself the first finding: a mature lane — 32 fixtures, 27 mutants, a 6,143-file corpus, the largest SFC corpus in the project — was unrepresented in M49, so nothing about it was discoverable from the ledger. Added here. ENTRY WAS NOT GREEN, DESPITE EVERY GATE READING PASS. Section A was red on exactly two unclassified types, ERROR and MISSING, and both were LIVE — 2.44% of sampled corpus files (10 of 410) carry recovery nodes, 55 ERROR and 5 MISSING, every MISSING the grammar's expected `>` terminator, and 8 of 12 deliberately malformed documents also produce ERROR. The precedent pointed the OTHER way and had to be set aside to see it: html ruled MISSING silent after twelve malformed documents produced none, toml ruled both silent because its grammar never emits them, and copying either would have been adopting a conclusion whose measurement had not been run. Svelte is the first lane in the project to rule MISSING handled. A REAL READ, INCOMPLETE. The analyzer's error walk iterated `namedChild`, and the expected `>` is an ANONYMOUS node, so it reported ERROR and was structurally blind to MISSING — the exact case it was written for. The engine's walk uses `children` and did report it, so nothing was lost operationally, but the three-part contract was honoured for one recovery type and silently not the other, and a contract that depends on a caller to be complete is not a contract. Now matches the engine; symbols and edges byte-identical, so the fix added a diagnostic and changed nothing else. F6 HAD THE SAME BLINDNESS, INVERTED. Its collector records `n.type`, and a MISSING node's type is the token the parser expected, so the literal `MISSING` never appeared — a lane that correctly HANDLED the type was reported uncovered, and could only have gone green by demoting it to silent, which is how a defect gets pinned. The collector now records the marker the way the analyzer does; it only ever adds, so no lane can newly fail from it. Pinned by `svelte/error-recovery` + mutant `svelte/recovery-stops-walk`, arranged so truncation cannot be faked: an unclosed `{#if}` makes the parser's ERROR span swallow the REST OF THE FILE, so valid markup sits inside the error region and a stopping walk publishes the module, one binding and one component while the document still looks analysed. No count-based gate can see that class. THE MUTANT WAS WEAKER THAN ITS OWN DESCRIPTION, and that was the more useful failure. The first version filtered relationships on `.range`, but relationships carry `line_number` — so it modelled symbol truncation alone while claiming both, and it still got caught. A mutant that does less than it claims is worse than none: it passes while testing a weaker contract. M12 READ 0.778 AGAINST A CORRECT ANALYZER. The truth had audited symbols and five relationship types and had NEVER audited `uses` or `references`, so 18 genuine edges read as fabrications — each verified against the source line it came from, then stated. Two limits recorded rather than smoothed: the candidate set was seeded by the analyzer's own output, so that direction cannot find a MISSED edge; and ten further edges stay `unknown` because their targets are function locals, parameters or store sigils, not component members. Now TP=81 FP=0 FN=0. THE AUDIT FOUND A REAL DEFECT THAT IS NOT THIS LANE'S. An identifier used as the RECEIVER of a method call loses its `uses` edge: `$: header = title.toUpperCase()` emits nothing, while `$: o = title.length` and `$: o = fn(title)` both emit theirs, and the same expression without the `$:` also loses it — isolated by A/B on one line, because property access survives, a call ARGUMENT survives, a call RECEIVER does not. A plain `.js` file reproduces it exactly, so svelte INHERITS it from the javascript sub-analyzer, whose lane is under active parallel work. Recorded as spec gap X1 with the owner named and deliberately NOT fixed here — editing another lane's live code to make this lane's gate green is the failure mode this project keeps naming — and deliberately absent from the M12 truth, because stating the missing edge would make the gate permanently red on a defect svelte does not own. `Card.svelte` carries it: `export let title` read in `$: header = title.toUpperCase()` and no edge produced. TWO CONTRACT RULINGS, both now RULED. D7 YES: a named function passed to a rune that INVOKES its argument is a call site — `$effect(fn)`, `$effect.pre(fn)`, `$effect.root(fn)`, `$effect.untracked(fn)`, `$derived.by(fn)` all emitted NOTHING before this, because the delegate suppresses the rune and its argument is an ordinary identifier no edge was made for, so a component's graph could not show it runs `fn` on every effect tick. The set is the INVOKING HALF of the rune surface and that split IS the ruling: `$derived(count)`, `$state(0)`, `$bindable(v)`, `$props()` take a value and never call it, and the read is already a `uses` edge, so refusing the call loses no data flow. An arrow argument is not a name, a member argument is an unresolved method, and a user's own `$`-prefixed function is not a rune. D8 YES, ratifying existing behaviour: `on:click={inc}`, `on:submit={() => save()}`, `on:click={box.open}` and `{@render row(it)}` all emit calls, dotted targets resolving to the LAST segment at three depths, which also closes the old D4 note that render tags and `on:` handlers once answered the same shape in opposite directions. THE CROSS-FAMILY DISAGREEMENT IS RECORDED, NOT SMOOTHED. The sibling vue lane emits NO calls for its equivalents — `@click="inc"` and `@submit="save()"` both produce nothing — so the two SFC siblings now differ on this ruling and nothing else measured. Vue's silence has the same shape as the under-claim and is NOT changed from here; aligning them is a separate ruling against the vue lane. A DEDUPE, MEASURED AND LEFT ALONE. Repeated (source, target, type) pairs collapse to one edge, so two call sites invoking the SAME function leave a single row and the other site is invisible. Pre-existing, shared across relationship types, and recorded in D7 beside the `#914` residual rather than fixed inside a contract ruling. It cost me a fixture and then a store assertion — both drafts pointed two emissions at one callee and so appeared to show the ruling not working, which is the second time this session a correct implementation looked broken because a test shared a name. Both now use distinct callees, and the D7/D8 pair is told apart by TARGET rather than by line. THE LANE HAD NO PIPE LEG AT ALL — the state html was in when every payload a rewrite introduced was verified only against the analyzer's return value. Eleven assertions now query the real brain.db through the real CLI: the component named from the STEM and not the filename (kind `class`, not `module` — my first assertion tested a kind this lane never claimed to emit), an `export let` prop as a property, a `$props()` binding declared exactly once, a `$:` reactive target, `instantiates`, BOTH new call sources, no NULL or non-positive line, and a prop default value never becoming a symbol name. `brain_relationship` has no target-name column, so the queries follow the same two cases the html leg distinguishes. Negative control: demanding a second rune call fails naming it. THE DOC WAS 51 LINES AND STALE where it mattered — 18/18 fixtures (now 34), `13 languages`, and nothing about the corpus, F5, M12, the error-recovery measurement or either ruling. A verification section reporting numbers from three review waves ago reads as current, which is worse than having none. Rewritten, with every number re-checked against the gates in the same pass. STATE: SPEC A–H 8/8 (76 types classified; gap list 16 CLOSED + 1 open cross-lane), F1 PASS, F3 34/34, F4 29/29, F5 100%/MISSING=0/unexplained=0 on both corpora, F6 PASS (34 handled, 78 types, 0 uncovered, 0 dead), M12 1.000/1.000 on 81 hand-audited facts, regex census 0, PIPE 11 store assertions with a working negative control, tsc clean. STILL NOT CLOSED, and the reason the row is `known-gap`: the canonical F5 ceremony has not run at a stable tree, so the baseline rows carry no truth totals and SPEC E/F rest on a scoped run rather than a pinned sweep — the user's ceremony, as for html and toml. Plus X1, owned by the javascript lane. WAVE 2 — THE CONSTRUCT CENSUS, AND WHAT IT FOUND. Asked again whether svelte was finished, having just learned in toml that a gate reading green because nobody ran it wide is not the same as a gate that is correct. Svelte's answer was worse than toml's: the lane had NO census at all, while html and toml each have one that consults neither the analyzer nor the oracle. So 34 fixtures, 29 mutants and F5 were all ONE author's reading of the same Svelte spec, and a construct both sides forgot could not appear as a disagreement. IT FOUND ONE IMMEDIATELY. The rune filter did not recognise `$state.eager` (15 corpus occurrences) or `$effect.pending` (11), so BOTH LEAKED: `$state.eager(0)` published `calls -> eager` and `$effect.pending()` published `calls -> pending` — framework plumbing named in the graph as though the component called it. The filter exists to prevent exactly this. THE F5 ORACLE MISSED THE SAME TWO RUNES FROM THE SAME SPEC, so analyzer and oracle AGREED and the lane read 100%. That is the measured reason the gate had to exist, not a hypothetical blind spot. THE FIX'S EFFECT IS ON THE PRIMARY GATE: at 1,000 files per corpus the svelte corpus's `unexplained` count went 2 -> 0, and nothing else changed. Those two rows I could not identify while `differential.ts` sat under the co-agent's uncommitted edit were exactly this defect; the count moving is what proves it. EXACT NAMES, NEVER LEAF SEGMENTS — load-bearing, not stylistic. The same `$name.member` shape is how ordinary user data is written: `$order.scoops` (6), `$value.foo` (6), `$a.foo` (5), `$formData.dob` (5), `$storeDeeper.items` (3), plus SvelteKit's `$lib` (3,549) and `$app` (25) — 78 distinct dotted forms in all. Adding the bare leaves would suppress `$my.eager` and `$my.pending`; I TRIED that repair as a negative control and it correctly FAILED, naming both. THE RULE THAT GIVES THE GATE TEETH: a plain 'classify every form' is vacuous behind a user-data fallback — 102 bare and 78 dotted forms would all pass. The binding rule is that a form whose BASE is a declared rune base must ITSELF be a declared rune, so `$state.anything` fails unless `anything` is enumerated. That is what caught the omission. REGISTERED AS A GATE rather than left as a script nobody runs: `audit:svelte-census` in package.json, in the verify chain beside the other two censuses, evidence identity M14.0.SVELTE-CENSUS in the honesty gate, and a lineage entry naming the census script and the svelte wasm but deliberately NOT the analyzer, because the gate does not consult it and claiming it would be a false lineage claim of exactly the kind this gate exists to catch. The honesty gate reports it all-green with 4 checks. THREE NEGATIVE CONTROLS EACH EXITING 1: un-declaring `$state.eager`; adding the bare leaves; declaring a non-rune absent from the corpus. The third I initially wrote BACKWARDS — I removed a declaration, but that check fires on a STALE one — and corrected it rather than counting it as a control that had passed. NO MUTANT FOR THIS CLASS, AND THAT IS THE FINDING. A harness transforms output; this defect is a missing SUPPRESSION, whose whole signature is an edge the analyzer chose NOT to emit, so reproducing it means ADDING an edge at a line the transform cannot know without reading source. My first attempt removed the edge instead and SURVIVED, because removing a fabricated edge makes a forbidding fixture pass more. Deleted rather than shipped — the same call made for toml's values-as-symbols mutant. What covers the class is the census's 20 positive suppression probes, which run the analyzer and assert an absence, the only direction able to see a missing suppression. The fixture pins both directions with LINE-SCOPED forbids, because `calls -> eager` is simultaneously the defect at L8 and a legitimate edge at L14 — a shape a target-only forbid cannot express. STILL OPEN AND NOT CLOSABLE FROM HERE: X1 (javascript analyzer — a `uses` edge lost whenever an identifier is the RECEIVER of a method call) and X2 (typescript oracle — `ctor.text` with no nameability guard, so `new class { ... }` publishes the class body as a name; the javascript twin already has the guard the TS side lacks). Both recorded with the fix specified, neither applied, both in files under active parallel edit. Plus the canonical F5 ceremony, which is the user's, and the depth figure ROTATES between runs, so a single run is not evidence of stability either way. WAVE 3 — THE CENSUS'S SECOND DIMENSION, AND THE WORST CLASS OF DEFECT. Asked to go deeper on the census, so the second dimension asks the same question of the TEMPLATE that the first asked of `$`-forms: is every `svelte:` tag and every block construct ruled? It found something the differential cannot see AT ALL. THE CORPUS CARRIES A TAG THAT CANNOT EXIST: `<svelte:selfdestructive x="{x - 1}"/>` in the project's own `compiler-errors/samples/svelte-selfdestructive/` — a deliberate near-miss of `svelte:self`, in a file the Svelte compiler REJECTS. The analyzer published `instantiates -> svelte:selfdestructive` and reported ZERO errors, because the grammar parses an unknown element name perfectly well; a name being ILLEGAL is not a parse failure. AND NO GATE COULD SEE IT. The oracle's condition is `!ORACLE_HTML_TAGS.has(name) && !VUE_STYLE_BUILTINS.has(name)`, and that name is in neither set — so the oracle derived the SAME edge. Both sides agreed, the differential reported 0 missing and 0 unexplained, and the lane read clean. This is the one class of defect invisible to the only gate that compares the two sides, BY CONSTRUCTION. The census argument is now demonstrated rather than asserted. RULED (D11): the `svelte:` prefix is a RESERVED NAMESPACE. Only the ten declared builtins exist; an undeclared `svelte:*` cannot name a component. Analyzer fixed; oracle side recorded as gap X4, one condition wide, not fixable from here because `differential.ts` is under active parallel edit. THE RULING IS A GATE, NOT A COMMENT — every `svelte:*` tag in the corpus must be a declared builtin or carry a REJECTED ruling, and a REJECTED ruling that no longer matches anything in the corpus FAILS AS STALE, so the rejection table cannot become a place to hide a construct that has since become legal. Two `{@tag}` invalid spellings in compiler-error samples are ruled rejected on the same argument. The block dimension is complete the same way: 15 constructs discovered, 13 declared with what each is FOR, 2 rejected, 0 unclassified, so a block type Svelte adds later fails here rather than being silently unhandled on both sides. SIX NEGATIVE CONTROLS NOW, each exiting 1 — the three rune ones plus dropping the REJECTED ruling, renaming a ruling to a name the corpus lacks, and REVERTING the analyzer's rule (caught as 'an undeclared member of the reserved namespace was PUBLISHED'). That last is the one that matters: it proves the census observes the ANALYZER, not just the corpus. A FIXTURE PINNING BOTH DIRECTIONS: `svelte/reserved-svelte-namespace` forbids the undeclared members and requires real components to be STILL published, because a rule that suppressed the whole `svelte:` neighbourhood would pass every forbid while destroying the lane — the same failure mode as the bare-leaf rune fix, caught by probing both ways. EXPECTED CONSEQUENCE, STATED SO THE NUMBER IS NOT MISREAD: once the analyzer stops publishing the edge, the oracle's row reads as MISSING rather than agreement, because a differential charges the analyzer for the truth's mistake. Svelte's depth figure is therefore EXPECTED to read 1 MISSING on any rotation containing that file, and that MISSING is X4, not an under-claim. Reporting it as 0 would mean hiding either the defect or the fix. STATE: census 7 checks all-green in the honesty gate, SPEC A-H 8/8, F1 PASS, F3 36/36, F4 29/29, F6 PASS, M12 1.000/1.000, all lanes' fixtures pass, full 1,121-mutant suite passes, tsc clean. STILL OPEN AND NOT CLOSABLE FROM HERE: X1 (javascript analyzer — a `uses` edge lost whenever an identifier is the RECEIVER of a method call; measured 36,353 such shapes across 994 of 1,500 sampled files, so this is a lane-scale change against a mature lane of 66 fixtures and 56 mutants, NOT a quick fix), X2 (typescript oracle — `ctor.text` with no nameability guard; a one-condition fix blocked only by the co-agent's uncommitted work in `differential.ts`), and X4 (svelte oracle — the reserved-namespace condition). All three recorded with the fix specified, none applied, all in files under active parallel edit. Plus the canonical F5 ceremony, which is the user's, and the depth figure ROTATES between runs.

issues.title: JavaScript construct census (M14.0.JS-CENSUS) + three documentation defects it exposed
issues.notes: Adds an 11-gate construct census for the javascript lane, registered as `audit:js-census` and wired into the verify chain. Discovery reads the CORPUS and the GRAMMAR only — it consults neither the analyzer's tables nor the oracle, because a construct BOTH of them forgot cannot appear as a disagreement. That is the X1 shape exactly: the defect WAS the agreement, so a gate that only compares the two sides cannot find it. The analyzer is consulted for the PROBES, which is a different job. THE GATE WITH TEETH: if a member chain's base is a declared global, every leaf under it must be declared, so `console.zzz` fails until `zzz` is enumerated. It fired immediately and correctly — 106 undeclared leaves under 15 reserved bases, a gap in the census's own table. The table is now derived from the sample the artifact publishes rather than hand-curated, and gate 9 PROBES a leaf of every non-console base so the table cannot rot into asserting suppression that no longer happens. ORPHAN POPULATION, wrong three times before it was right: 'name is not a contains SOURCE' reported 99% (that is the owner set); excluding nothing useful reported 94.7%; excluding module-scope roots reported 93.6% with function-LOCAL samples, which the containment contract has never covered. The gate passed on all three because it only asserted orphanTotal > 0, so it could not notice a figure moving eightfold. Read off the contract itself the result is sharp and CONFIRMS M49 JD3's predicted split: CLASS members 0/11 unplaced, OBJECT-LITERAL methods 92/92. That refines JD3 — its class-member half no longer holds on this corpus, so JD3 is an object-literal finding now. THREE DOC DEFECTS FOUND. (1) MINE, published one commit earlier and corrected here: I claimed the enum's `imports` label carries the wire value `brain_import` and that an `imports` allowlist entry therefore matches no analyzer edge on ANY lane — an invented cross-lane defect. There are two enums: `types.ts` has `Imports = "brain_import"`, which is the SQLITE TABLE name, and `engine.ts` has `Imports = "imports"`, which is the wire value. I read one enum and assumed it was the only one. (2) Pre-existing: the `calls` row claimed 'builtins filtered (console.*, Object leaf methods)'; only the console half holds — 27 probed global leaves are all named, `Object.keys({})` publishes `calls keys` AND `uses Object`. (3) Pre-existing and with teeth: the symbol table claimed a private field `#x` collapses to `x`; it does not — `legacy-client.js` publishes `#events` and `Svelte4Component->#events`. A census that stripped the `#` while matching containment targets reported 92 of 96 class members as unplaced, a wholly invented defect. TWO HONEST NON-FINDINGS, recorded rather than acted on: `NaN`/`Infinity` are global VALUES so naming them is correct (an early draft asserting silence was the gate being wrong), and `module`/`exports`/`require` are not suppressible bases at all — `require()` is the CJS import edge and `module.exports` the CJS export edge, so enumerating them as builtins would have demanded suppressing two of the lane's most correct edges. M12 IMPACT, measured by A/B on identical fixtures: precision and recall are UNCHANGED at 0.973 with and without the X1 analyzer fix, and the fix adds 8 genuinely new receiver edges that the 112 hand-audited M12 facts do not list, moving `unknown` 62 -> 69. Adding them as relationship facts was tried and REVERTED: their targets are free variables rather than declared symbols, so the schema cannot resolve them and recall fell to 0.901. `unknown` is their honest bucket, the same category as the 3 pre-existing `node:*` import false negatives.

issues.notes: SUPERSEDED, 2026-09-28. This entry recorded that script/m14/mutate-analyzer.ts had four syntax errors at HEAD and at every one of the twelve most recent commits touching it, so F4 had not run for the whole visible history and any F4 number rested on a gate that could not execute. **IT NOW RUNS.** The co-agent repaired the registry: the file parses with 0 errors, carries ONE `MUTANTS` declaration (the duplicate is gone, as predicted), and holds 1,327 entries. `BB_MUTANT_ONLY=javascript/ bun run script/m14/mutate-analyzer.ts` reports all 56 javascript mutants caught. **SO MY EARLIER STATEMENT IS OUTDATED AND SHOULD BE READ AS SPENT:** I told the user that the javascript 56/56 was not a claim I could stand behind. That was true when written and is false now. The entry is kept rather than deleted because the inventory is what made the repair checkable — the duplicate declaration, the truncated transform, the two stray braces — and the count moved from two disjoint arrays (35 + 1282 = 1317) to 1,327 entries, which is 10 more than the union I computed, so the co-agent added mutants while repairing rather than only merging. **WHAT SURVIVES FROM THE ORIGINAL FINDING.** Two things, and neither is the breakage itself. First, the reverted partial repair: I had merged the two arrays and repaired three of the four syntax sites, verified each in isolation, and then reverted rather than ship a 1,317-entry merge of a mutation gate that had never executed — because a wrong transform does not crash, it stops catching its own defect. That judgement is unchanged by the co-agent's repair; the work simply got done properly rather than by me. Second, and more valuable: the class of damage was SILENT. A duplicate JSON key, two duplicate array declarations, a truncated transform and a differential that could not load all presented as green. Every 'all green' in this project is conditional on the gates actually executing, which is exactly why a gate that cannot fail and a gate that cannot run are the same failure wearing different clothes.

waves.method: W8 had wired F6 for the first time and it promptly failed on 24 analyzer literals across java/javascript/cpp/go/zig that are neither node types in the pinned grammar nor spec-classified - F6 calls that dead code, the class 'the branch can never fire'. Each literal was adjudicated from the grammars themselves, not from reading the analyzer: (1) is it in the grammar's raw symbol enumeration including the underscore-prefixed hidden rules; (2) does it occur anywhere in the language's fixture corpus (all children, anonymous included); (3) can a targeted source that exercises the construct produce it. A separate risk was settled first because it would have invalidated every verdict: WHICH grammar does the analyzer load - the M14 harness and the production path (bbWasmCandidates -> <repo>/wasm/...) both resolve to the vendored wasm/ dir, so the probe grammar is production's grammar. Verdict: all 24 grammar-dead. The deciding question was then whether each dead branch carried weight, and exactly one did: java's argument-count guard skipped a node type named 'comment' that tree-sitter-java does not define (comments are line_comment/block_comment), so the skip never fired and `g(1 /* c */, 2)` reported argumentCount 3 - a live defect in the payload a consumer uses to tell overloads apart. The java annotation-name fallback and the js property_signature disjunct were redundant dead names (removed, doc corrected); the cpp/go/zig removals and re-pointings are provably behaviour-preserving (a name that matches no node type cannot change a branch) and that is measured, not argued: the zig edge set over all 90 .zig files of the zls corpus is byte-identical before and after. One dead literal was a whole no-op function (zig hasZigQualifiedAncestor, whose only true return referenced a type that cannot exist). The zig literal list also exposed a REAL defect - the scope model binds every identifier under a parameter node, so names that appear only in a parameter's TYPE become bindings and suppress genuine reads (probe-verified: zero uses edges where one is required, e.g. a struct type field named FLAG shadowing a file-level const FLAG) - whose fix was written, measured, and HELD: it removes the accidental shadowing and thereby exposes a second pre-existing gap (signature-region names surfacing as bare value reads), and the in-flight oracle DERIVES those reads, so landing the analyzer half alone would leave the two contradicting. The analyzer's behaviour is verified exactly unchanged and the defect is registered. Closing this also exposed a gate bug in F6 itself: it read analyzer source as raw text, so an audit note quoting a removed literal counted as a live one - the gate would keep a removed literal dead forever precisely because it was documented. F6 now scans comment-masked source with a --selftest that proves (positionally, per gated language) that every removed occurrence is inside a comment, that masking never invents a literal, and that the gate can still fail. F6's findings are resolved, so its G8 register row is removed and the producer is wired.

waves.title: Groovy continuation shapes (#851/#852): a paren-less leading-dot continuation stops fabricating a call edge, a dotted juxt callee stops duplicating a method as two graph nodes — and the calls oracle that was blind to both is corrected
waves.method: Two findings filed while building the M59 line fixture (groovy/lines-825), each reproduced through the real analyzer at HEAD with the raw tree printed beside the emitted edges, so the emitting branch was identified rather than guessed. The discriminating fact is measured, not assumed: `leading_dot_call` carries an `arguments` field iff the continuation has an argument list (`.build(1)` yes, `.label` no), so one rule separates the call from the member read. Each shape was then pinned beside its own ONE-LINE control in one fixture, because the control is the contract — the same chain written on one line and written across a continuation must emit the same calls multiset, and a member access must stay a read. The oracle half was not optional: before this round deriveGroovyEdges had no leading_dot_call branch at all and gave the juxt call the whole dotted text, i.e. it mirrored the defect rather than the contract.

findings.note: A newline-continued property access (`this` / `        .label`) is an extremely common Groovy layout, and the pinned grammar shapes it as its own `leading_dot_call` statement node with NO argument list. The branch emitted `calls -> label` for every continuation regardless, so the property read became a CALL and the read itself vanished (the same access on one line emits `uses A -> label`). Fixed by the argument-list discriminator: with `arguments` a genuine call (`.build(1)`, unchanged), without it a member READ in the exact shape collectFieldAccessUses uses, attributed to the enclosing METHOD because the continuation node does not carry its receiver (the GAD1 convention for an unresolvable receiver — hence `uses A -> label` at line 5 and `uses continuedRead -> label` at line 11 deliberately name different owners for the same member). Measured on the pinned 400-file grails-core sample: 57 paren-less continuations in 22 files (5.5%), i.e. 57 fabricated calls and 57 lost reads, against 217 paren-ful continuations that were already correct. Pinned by fixture groovy/continuation-shapes-851; mutant groovy/parenless-continuation-call is CAUGHT (0 -> 5 failures).
findings.severityDetail: A false CALL edge to a property name creates a dependency that does not exist and loses the read that does — wrong in both directions at once.

findings.note: A continued dotted call folds into `juxt_function_call name: (field_access ...)`, which produced three defects from one shape: (1) the call TARGET was the whole dotted text, so `helper.build` and `build` became two graph nodes for one method (the family contract, and this analyzer's own method_invocation branch, is the BARE callee leaf); (2) a field_access in callee position leaked a `uses -> build` READ, contradicting the family rule that a callee is not a read (java/kotlin/scala all suppress it, and so does this shape written on one line). Measured: 60 dotted juxt callees in 38 of 400 files (9.5%), against 228 plain ones already correct. Fixed by taking the leaf (`nameNode.field` when the name is a field_access) with the leaf's own line (#825), and by suppressing the callee-position field_access. The edge now also carries `groovyCallExpression` — the callee as written — mirroring the sibling method_invocation branch, so the dotted form stays recoverable downstream even though the target names the leaf. Pinned by fixture groovy/continuation-shapes-851; mutants groovy/juxt-target-dotted and groovy/juxt-callee-read are both CAUGHT, and each is caught by THAT FIXTURE ALONE - the measurement that nothing in the suite could see this class before the round.
findings.severityDetail: One method silently became two graph nodes and the callee appeared as a member read, so both navigation and read-accounting were wrong on the same statement.
